findings.title: Blind glob copy with no validation of copied sources
findings.message: glob("*.go") copies every Go file, including *_test.go files for the notebook package. The mapping replaces only the full import path. Test files that use external test packages or other internal references may break. Additionally, `cmd/notes` files copied into the root are `package main`, but any non-main-package test files would conflict. Unsorted glob order is harmless, but the tool silently copies nothing if the directory is empty.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly assert that at least one file was copied per source. Validate the generated module with `go vet ./...` in the stage before renaming.

findings.title: Locale-dependent file encoding
findings.message: read_text and write_text use the locale default encoding, so non-UTF-8 locales can corrupt or fail on Go sources, which are UTF-8.
findings.suggestion: Pass encoding="utf-8" to read_text and write_text.

findings.title: Fragile string surgery on main.go may produce non-compiling code
findings.message: The rewrite of main.go relies on text.index() for exact substrings. If the source main.go changes, index raises an unhelpful ValueError mid-staging. It also assumes `errors` is already imported, and removes the `path/filepath` import without checking whether filepath is still used elsewhere. The generated app may fail to compile.
findings.suggestion: Check that the markers exist and fail with a clear error. Verify the generated sources compile, for example by running `go build` or `go vet` in the stage, or add imports with goimports. Prefer a dedicated template file over string surgery.
findings.evidence: text = text[:start] + '\tif *directory == "" { return errors.New("supply -data-dir with an absolute private application directory") }\n' + text[end:]
